### Problem: subtree sizes after reparenting {#sec-tr-p4-sizes}

::: {.p-statement}
`parent[0] = -1` and the array is a tree on vertices $0..n-1$. `s[i]` is a lowercase letter. At the same moment, every $x \ge 1$ whose original ancestors include the same letter adopts the closest such ancestor as its new parent. Return the subtree size of every node in the new tree.

Constraints: $1 \le n \le 10^5$.

Source: [LC 3331 · Find Subtree Sizes After Changes](https://leetcode.com/problems/find-subtree-sizes-after-changes/){.solved difficulty="Medium"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
The new parent of $x$ is an original ancestor, so a DFS of the original tree sees that ancestor before $x$. While the DFS is inside $x$, the vertices entered and not yet left are exactly the ancestors. `last[c]` remembers the deepest of them with letter $c$. Restore it when the DFS leaves $x$, and the sibling sees the path without $x$.
:::

::: {#fig-tr-reparent}

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):

    root = V.Node("a", [
        V.Node("b", [V.Node("a", color="green"), V.Node("b"), V.Node("c")]),
        V.Node("a", color="green"),
    ], color="green")
    V.tree(ax, p, root, dx=1.15, dy=1.35, size=10)
    V.array(ax, p, [6, 3, 1, 1, 1, 1], y=-5.0, label="size")

V.show(draw)
```

Letters `abaabc`, in the order the nodes are drawn. The shaded nodes hold `a`. The subtree sizes after the reparenting are $6, 3, 1, 1, 1, 1$.

:::

::: {.p-approach}
1. **Climb.** For each vertex, walk up until the same letter, then walk up the new parents adding $1$ to every node on the chain. Correct, and $O(n \cdot h)$. A path of one letter is about $n^2 / 2$ steps.
2. **One cell per letter.** Iterative DFS with an exit event stored under the children. On entry, `last[s[x]]` is the new parent if it is not $-1$. Subtree sizes add in the reverse of the entry order. $O(n)$, and the stack is explicit.

**Invariant.** `last[c]` is the deepest ancestor with letter $c$, or $-1$ if none. The exit event restores the value from before this node, so the invariant holds for the next sibling.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Climb

::: {.form-next}
The definition, written as two walks. Use it to check the fast form on small trees. Do not submit it at $n = 10^5$.
:::


::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
def subtree_sizes_climb(parent, s):
    n = len(parent)
    new_par = parent[:]
    for x in range(1, n):
        v = parent[x]
        while v != -1 and s[v] != s[x]:
            v = parent[v]
        if v != -1:
            new_par[x] = v
    sz = [0] * n
    for x in range(n):
        v = x
        while v != -1:
            sz[v] += 1
            v = new_par[v]
    return sz
```

##### C++

```cpp
vector<int> subtreeSizesClimb(const vector<int>& parent, const string& s) {
    int n = (int)parent.size();
    vector<int> np = parent, sz(n);
    for (int x = 1; x < n; ++x) {
        int v = parent[x];
        while (v != -1 && s[v] != s[x]) v = parent[v];
        if (v != -1) np[x] = v;
    }
    for (int x = 0; x < n; ++x)
        for (int v = x; v != -1; v = np[v]) ++sz[v];
    return sz;
}
```

:::

#### One cell per letter

::: {.form-next}
Keep the same new parent, and find it in $O(1)$ from the path the DFS is already on. `ENTER = -2` because a restored `last` value can be $-1$, which would look like a real parent.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get('sizes', 'cell')
    assert str(final) == '[6, 3, 1, 1, 1, 1]'
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
def subtree_sizes(parent, s):
    n = len(parent)
    ch = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    for i in range(1, n):
        ch[parent[i]].append(i)
    new_par = parent[:]
    order = []
    last = [-1] * 26
    enter = -2
    st = [(0, enter)]
    while st:
        u, tag = st.pop()
        c = ord(s[u]) - 97
        if tag != enter:
            last[c] = tag
            continue
        if last[c] != -1:
            new_par[u] = last[c]
        st.append((u, last[c]))
        last[c] = u
        order.append(u)
        for v in reversed(ch[u]):
            st.append((v, enter))
    sz = [1] * n
    for k in range(n - 1, 0, -1):
        sz[new_par[order[k]]] += sz[order[k]]
    return sz


assert subtree_sizes([-1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1], "abaabc") == [6, 3, 1, 1, 1, 1]
assert subtree_sizes([-1, 0, 4, 0, 1], "abbba") == [5, 2, 1, 1, 1]
assert subtree_sizes([-1], "a") == [1]
assert subtree_sizes([-1, 0], "aa") == [2, 1]
for n in range(1, 12):
    parent = [-1] + [random.randrange(i) for i in range(1, n)]
    letters = "".join(chr(97 + random.randrange(3)) for _ in range(n))
    assert subtree_sizes(parent, letters) == subtree_sizes_climb(parent, letters)
```

##### C++

```cpp
vector<int> subtreeSizes(const vector<int>& parent, const string& s) {
    int n = (int)parent.size();
    vector<vector<int>> ch(n);
    for (int i = 1; i < n; ++i) ch[parent[i]].push_back(i);
    vector<int> np = parent, order, sz(n, 1);
    int last[26];
    fill(last, last + 26, -1);
    const int ENTER = -2;
    vector<pair<int, int>> st = {{0, ENTER}};
    while (!st.empty()) {
        auto [u, tag] = st.back();
        st.pop_back();
        int c = s[u] - 'a';
        if (tag != ENTER) { last[c] = tag; continue; }
        if (last[c] != -1) np[u] = last[c];
        st.push_back({u, last[c]});
        last[c] = u;
        order.push_back(u);
        for (int v : ch[u]) st.push_back({v, ENTER});
    }
    for (int k = n - 1; k >= 1; --k) sz[np[order[k]]] += sz[order[k]];
    return sz;
}
```

:::

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Climb** is $O(n \cdot h)$ time. **One cell per letter** enters and leaves each vertex once: $O(n)$ time and $O(n)$ memory, plus $26$ cells. The reverse accumulation stops before the root, because `new_par[0]` is $-1$.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- One node returns `[1]`. Nothing moves.
- `[-1,0]` and `"aa"` keeps the parent: the parent is already the closest `a`. Sizes `[2,1]`.
- `[-1,0,1]` and `"aba"` moves node $2$ onto $0$, skipping $1$. Sizes `[3,1,1]`.
- A path of one letter does not move. Sizes are $n, n-1, \ldots, 1$. The climb form is the one that dies there.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistakes"}
- Searching the new parents, instead of the original ancestors, changes who a later vertex can see. Compute every new parent from the original tree first.
- Forgetting to restore `last` makes the next sibling adopt this node. The exit puts the old value back.
- Adding sizes from the largest label downward assumes a parent has a smaller label. In `[-1, 0, 4, 0, 1]` the parent of $2$ is $4$. Use the traversal order.
:::

**Variants.** The minutes until every employee has heard are a root-path sum of the managers' delays: [LC 1376 · Time Needed to Inform All Employees](https://leetcode.com/problems/time-needed-to-inform-all-employees/){difficulty="Medium"}. The closest ancestor with a larger value is the same path, kept as a stack that is restored on the way out. Subtree sizes with no reparenting are [CSES 1674 · Subordinates](https://cses.fi/problemset/task/1674).
